title: Unify minimal auth handshake and streamline streaming iterators across SDKs
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: SDKs had divergent lightweight auth handshakes and several slightly different async iterator APIs for streaming. This caused parity bugs (timeouts that only showed up in Go), awkward ergonomic differences in TypeScript consumer code, and duplicated retry logic. This PR introduces a small, intentionally minimal common handshake shim and a thin stream-wrapping adapter implemented in Python/TS/Go to normalize iterator behavior and retry policy wiring. Scope: - Add a minimal cross-language auth handshake contract (opaque token preflight + agreed timeout window) and adapters for each SDK. - Introduce StreamWrapper (Py/TS/Go) that presents a consistent async iterator/async generator/pull API and surfaces a single retry profile entrypoint. - Replace ad-hoc timeout and reauth calls in SDKs with the shim; preserve previous behavior as a compatibility opt-in via an explicit flag. - Bump SDK package versions: py 0.6.3 -> 0.6.4, ts 1.8.0 -> 1.8.1, go v1.3.1 -> v1.3.2. High level changes per SDK: - Python: new redwood.sdk.auth.minimal_handshake module (handshake.py), StreamWrapper class in redwood.sdk.streaming.adapter, small rework of async generator helpers, added unit tests and an integration test against the local dev runtime. - TypeScript: introduce compact handshake interface and streamWrap helper in src/stream/wrap.ts, exported types to improve TS ergonomics, adjust existing retry builder to accept the unified profile object. - Go: add handshake.go; implement stream adapter that exposes a channel-based iterator and a PullNext(ctx) method; adjust retry wiring to use the shared policy. Commits (summary): [1/5] introduce minimal auth contract and docs; [2/5] Python adapter + tests; [3/5] TypeScript adapter + types and examples; [4/5] Go adapter + channel iterator; [5/5] release bumps, changelogs, and cross-sdk integration test. Files changed (high-level): - redwood/sdk/auth/handshake.md - redwood/sdk/auth/handshake.py - redwood/sdk/streaming/adapter.py - py tests/integration/test_handshake.py - packages/sdk-js/src/stream/wrap.ts - packages/sdk-js/src/auth/handshake.ts - packages/sdk-go/handshake.go - packages/sdk-go/stream/adapter.go - tests/interop/session_handshake_matrix.yml - package version updates and changelogs Rationale and compatibility: The handshake is intentionally minimal: an exchange to confirm token validity window and suggested heartbeat interval. We preserve older auth flows; the new behavior is behind a config flag enable_minimal_handshake and will be enabled by default for new SDK releases. This keeps backward compatibility while reducing subtle race conditions in reauth under high concurrency. Testing and CI: Ran full unit suite across Py/TS/Go. The PR initially hit a flaky test in go stream adapter (race on channel close) during the first CI run; the adapter was hardened and CI was re-run. Final CI summary is green with coverage increase in streaming modules. Upgrade notes: - TypeScript: consumers should replace manual iterator helpers with streamWrap(...) for simpler error handling; migration examples added to CHANGELOG. - Python: StreamWrapper is an additive API and a drop-in for most async generator uses. - Go: new PullNext(ctx) API included; existing helper still supported for one release. Related: ENG-9832 (centralize lightweight reauth policy), ENG-9870 (stream ergonomics parity). Merge: squash and merge to main.
